waputikia.observation: Personally read ROM morphology/taxonomy and inspected ROM61105 isolated branch, ROM61114 fine sprays and USNM35409 syntype actual photo thumbnails. Thick finite axis, irregular stout branches rapidly dichotomizing to fine terminal sprays. ROM says affinity uncertain; listed Rhodophyta is not treated as resolved. These are low-resolution actual specimen photos, not ROM model; no complete parent/attachment inferred.
waputikia.claim: Waputikia ramosa fossil-specimen morphological concept only, not whole living organism, exact museum replica or resolved algal affinity.
features: Uneven stout lateral branches with rapid dichotomous taper into fine terminal sprays
Asymmetrical preserved specimen relief, no root holdfast leaves or tree foliage
Thin irregular shale support with no assertion of exact specimen outline
waputikia.decisions: Concept branching too tree-like in secondary sprays; implement rapid thick-to-fine subdivision and asymmetrical broad fine fans. Broken finite axis ends, no attachment. Back is original plain shale; slab is interpretive support. Relief thickness exaggerated for reading at512px, not literal fossil relief measurement.

linear-dune.observation: Read Lancaster NPS article morphology. Personally inspected Figure5 actual composite pixels: panelD simple long parallel linear Kalahari dunes, panelE complex linear; caption conflicts with prose letter indexing. Use panelD with length/sinuosity and two flanks, not panelC parabolic. Copyright2009 GSA figure consult-only.
linear-dune.claim: Generic original longitudinal linear sand dune process/form illustration, no named site, era, exact dimensions or wind reconstruction.
features: Single very elongated narrow sinuous longitudinal crest
Both exposed sloping flanks and finite tapering ends
Irregular crest height without transverse wave rows, U or star arms
Sand primary mass, subordinate cutaway support
linear-dune.decisions: Retain concept long S crest, two flanks, no ripple belts. Keep crest mostly continuous and narrow. Palette faceting subordinate to silhouette. Original bottom and end caps form closed volume. Nominal landscape scale artistic, not sampled locality.

kettle-basin.observation: Personally read NPS kettle formation by buried detached glacial ice melt, shallow closed pit in sediment, often pond. Inspected JohnGood LamarValley pond and JacobFrank Kennicott depressions: irregular sediment slopes and hummocky setting, no construction of volcanic rim.
kettle-basin.claim: Generic closed kettle depression in hummocky glacial sediment with shallow partial pond, no exact locality, ice age or physical measurement asserted.
features: Closed basin floor below all surrounding sediment
Uneven low hummocks in glacial till, no elevated volcanic circular rim
Partial shallow water with exposed irregular inward slopes
Sparse irregularly embedded stones subordinate to terrain
kettle-basin.decisions: Concept read as depression not crater; retain asymmetry and broad gentle glacial sediment hummocks. Avoid evenly spaced ring/tile patterns. Water opaque simplified teaching surface below surrounding ground, sediment floor exists below it. Closed irregular cutaway block bottom.

rimstone-dam.observation: Read MammothCave RimstoneDams paragraph and GreatBasin CaveGeologyInDepth rimstone paragraphs53-55: calcite rich water flows over crest, increasing dam, pool behind. Inspected ThomasDiGiovannangelo actual MammothCave dam photograph: thin sinuous irregular crest attached to floor, not geometric regular rings.
rimstone-dam.claim: Generic original ONE thin sinuous calcite dam enclosing ONE small cave pool on attached cave floor, no named cave, age or exact real-world dimensions.
features: ONE continuous thin sinuous mineral wall enclosing ONE pool
Thin uneven crest above pool level and steep outer wall
Wall attached to original cave floor
No scaled nested bowls or repeated terrace stacks
rimstone-dam.decisions: Concept wall slightly thick; reduce relative crest thickness while preserving readability, vary curvature nonperiodically. Single closed sinuous enclosure, not a terrace set. Back and underside original floor. Water stylized opaque blue-green volume, no transparency complexity or physical depth claim.
